title: Club sandwich on white bread with cheese

content.title: About
content.content: A club sandwich on white bread with cheese consists of three layers of toasted white bread, between which are placed ham, turkey, bacon, lettuce, tomato and melted cheese. The sandwich is usually served cut into quarters and often accompanied by fries or chips.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The club sandwich originated in the United States in the early 20th century and quickly became a fast‑food staple.
The classic recipe includes three types of meat, but vegetarian versions replace them with plant‑based alternatives.
White bread gives the sandwich a soft texture, though it can be swapped for whole‑grain bread for a healthier option.
The sandwich is often served with mayo or mustard, enhancing its flavor profile.
Some restaurants add avocado or a fried egg yolk for extra creaminess.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: Ham, turkey and bacon provide high‑quality protein needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Calcium content
items.content: Cheese is a good source of calcium, supporting bone and tooth health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The meat and bread contain vitamins B1, B2, B6 and B12, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Lettuce and tomato add fiber, which aids normal digestion.

items.title: Iron
items.content: Meat and cheese supply iron, essential for oxygen transport in the blood.

items.title: High sodium
items.content: Ham, bacon and cheese are often high in salt, which can be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Bacon and cheese are rich in saturated fats that may raise cholesterol levels when consumed in excess.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese can trigger allergic reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: A club sandwich is calorie‑dense; portion control is advisable, especially on a weight‑management diet.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Meat ingredients must be properly stored and cooked to avoid food‑borne illness.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The sandwich is typically eaten by hand, cutting each quarter apart. It can be dressed with additional sauces, mustard or mayo to taste. For a lighter version, swap bacon for turkey and use whole‑grain bread.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Prepared sandwich can be kept in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours in an airtight container. If components are stored separately, keep meat items at ≤4 °C and bread in a dry place to prevent sogginess.
